habitat: Pairs, sometimes small groups, near river bridges, dam walls, gorges and buildings, seldom far from water. It perches on dead trees in the water and on bridge rails.
summary: A fairly common wetland resident. Full orange cap, entirely white underparts except a narrow darker line on the lower flanks, and wire-like tail-shafts that are hard to see in flight. From a perch it repeats chirrik-weet. In flight it says chit-chit. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Pearl-breasted Swallow is blue on the head and has no tail-shafts. Wire-tailed Swallow has an orange cap and wire-like tail-shafts.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

underparts.pattern: Entirely white, except a narrow darker line on the lower flanks.

tail.shape: Wire-like tail-shafts, difficult to see in flight.

calls.description: A twittering chirrik-weet from a perch, and chit-chit in flight. Grade A call from Chiang Dao, Thailand. The filename names Wire-tailed Swallow.
